Internal rename in @workspace/shared: the run goals API schema becomes runGoalsResponseSchema and the database schema takes the name runGoalsSchema, so the API schema no longer shadows the database one. No behaviour change.

Server-side Sparky chat (and MCP) tools, so the same on web, iOS and Android chat: a training review (training_review: sessions per week, stalled lifts, RPE/RIR effort, muscle coverage) and a run review (run_review: runs per week, weekly distance and jumps over 10%, pace against the period before, training load and recovery) in the exercise stats tool; propose_plan_changes / apply_plan_changes in the workout plan tool (planned-weight changes with reasons, applied only after the user confirms); and sparky_review_calorie_target (read-only check of the calorie target against adaptive TDEE and weight trend). new_feature.name: Training, run, plan and calorie target reviews in Sparky chat
new_feature.description: Ask Sparky how your training or running is going and it reads the last 4 weeks (7 to 90 days on request): for strength, sessions per week, lifts that have stalled, effort from logged RPE/RIR and muscle coverage; for running, runs per week, weekly distance and jumps, pace against the period before and training load with a recovery hint. It can also propose planned-weight changes for the active workout plan (add a step, lighten or hold, each with its reason) and apply only the ones you agree to, and check whether the calorie target fits your estimated maintenance and weight trend. These are chat tools on the server, so they work the same in web and phone chat and through MCP.

summary: Weather for GPS-recorded activities. A new external provider type, Weather (Open-Meteo compatible), is added on the web in Settings > External Providers (server URL, optional API key, privacy and free-tier notes). When the phone app uploads an activity's GPS track the server looks up the temperature and conditions at the start (rounded start place and time) and stores them on the entry, unless it already has weather (e.g. from Garmin). The phone app's activity detail (cardio session stats) gains a Weather tile (°F with the miles/imperial setting); the web activity report already showed weather when present. Configuring the provider is web-only.

new_feature.name: Weather for GPS-recorded activities
new_feature.description: With a weather provider of the type Weather (Open-Meteo compatible) added in web Settings > External Providers (or shared by the admin or a family member), the server looks up the temperature and conditions at the start of each new GPS-recorded walk, run or ride after its route is saved, sending only the start time and the start place rounded to about 1 km. Activities that already have weather, such as Garmin imports, keep it. The phone app shows it as a Weather tile on the activity's detail (in °F with imperial units) and the web shows it in the activity report. The provider can only be set up on the web; activities are GPS-recorded only in the phone app.

summary: iOS/Apple Watch permission fix. On the watch, the workout effort score permission is no longer requested when a workout starts; it is checked right before the rating is written and requested then if Health does not report it granted, so the 1-10 rating is saved instead of refused. The watch run asks for the workout route permission only while it is not granted. On the iPhone, the workout route type (like the effort type) is no longer counted as an unrequested Health permission, so the permission sheet stops reappearing on every visit. No audit row or note changes in substance; it makes the Apple Watch effort rating in the 'Workout effort score (1-10)' new feature actually save.

Device Projection (TDEE) now uses one device total-calorie figure per day from Health Connect, Garmin or Polar, in that fixed order (never summed; zero totals skipped), instead of Health Connect only. Apple Health totals are still left out on purpose. The labels on web and mobile change from 'Health Connect total calories' to 'Device total calories' and the settings texts name Health Connect, Garmin or Polar.

new_feature.name: Zone 2 base running program
new_feature.description: A ten-week base-building program, 3 or 4 easy runs a week, where each run targets your Zone 2 heart rate range (from your heart rate zone settings) instead of a pace, with lighter weeks 4 and 8, strides in weeks 6, 7 and 9 and zone-check runs in weeks 4, 8 and 10. While recording, the phone shows the range and, with an Apple Watch or Wear OS watch supplying heart rate, says whether you are in, above or below Zone 2 and alerts when you stay outside it (allowing for warm-up and drift); without a watch it falls back to the talk test. A program run started on either watch holds the same range. The web lists and runs the program on its Training programs page and calendar but has no heart rate guidance and cannot record it.

summary: Server only: each backup is built in a private work directory and published whole, so a crash or overlapping run no longer leaves partial archives that retention counted as backups. The admin backup settings and actions are unchanged.

Server only: the /mfa-factors per-IP rate limit (5 per 30 s) now uses the shared makeIpRateLimit factory, so its window resets when it ends instead of the inline limiter's sweep-dependent reset. Sign-in screens are unchanged.

Server only: on shutdown the server lets running cron jobs and bulk imports finish and releases provider sync claims (gracefulShutdown, shutdownHooks, providerSyncClaim), so a restart no longer leaves syncs stuck as claimed. No UI change.

iOS/Apple Watch: stop asking for the workout effort permission repeatedly.
